chunks: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said:
It was said to al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام: “How did you wake this morning, O son of the Messenger of Allah?”

He said: “I awoke while I have a Lord above me, the Fire before me, death pursuing me, and the reckoning surrounding me. I am held in pledge by my deeds. I do not find what I love, nor do I repel what I dislike. Affairs are in the hand of another than me: if He wills, He punishes me, and if He wills, He pardons me. So what poor person is poorer than me?”

key_terms.النَّارُ أَمَامِي: The Hellfire before me; awareness of possible punishment in the afterlife.
key_terms.الْحِسَابُ مُحْدِقٌ بِي: The reckoning encircling me; being surrounded by accountability before Allah.
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ يَطْلُبُنِي: Death pursuing me; the nearness and inevitability of death.
key_terms.رَبٌّ فَوْقِي: My Lord above me; a direct expression of divine lordship and human servitude.
key_terms.عَفَا عَنِّي: He pardoned me; divine forgiveness and mercy.
key_terms.فَقِيرٍ: Poor; here indicating utter neediness and dependence before Allah.
key_terms.مُرْتَهَنٌ بِعَمَلِي: Held in pledge by my deeds; one’s actions bind one to their consequences.

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام describe the believer’s condition before Allah, death, and the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a deeply humble and spiritually alert description of the human condition before Allah. Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام speaks of divine lordship, death, the Fire, and reckoning to emphasize dependence on Allah and accountability for one’s deeds. Its significance lies in cultivating humility, awareness of the afterlife, and recognition that all affairs ultimately rest with Allah.
